<a id="mission"></a>

## Mission

You build ONE unit: the HUMAN SKIN. Port pocs/human-render into fs3-cli behind the frozen render seam so a person at a terminal sees beautiful output on every covered verb, while every pipe, file, CI log and agent keeps receiving the byte-identical JSON envelope it receives today. You also own the agent-path documentation for the new default (ac-0005) and the `add` progress meter on stderr. The renderer's ONLY input is an envelope: a fact a human needs that the envelope does not carry is a gap in the CONTRACT to report, never something to fetch on the side. You report to the PM (pij-near-carp), not to prime.

Its LEARNINGS.md §1 justifies every crate and §4 gives the port order; §1's three gotchas (custom_styling implies tty so call force_no_tty(), comfy-table 8 renamed the preset API so every online snippet is v7, nested styles eat their parent so style segments independently) will each cost you an hour if you rediscover them. pocs/** is READ-ONLY: port from it, never edit it. |
| u2 | The seam is FROZEN and you FILL it, never widen it: `fs3_cli::render::render(&Envelope&lt;Value&gt;) -&gt; Option&lt;String&gt;` (crates/cli/src/render.rs). Dispatch on (ok, command) — `ok` is the only discriminator, so one failure surface serves every verb. Returning None means decline, and emit() prints the JSON instead: that is the honest fallthrough for any verb you do not cover, and it must never become a panic or a blank screen. You do NOT touch emit()'s serialise-first ordering, fs3_core::output::resolve, or envelope production anywhere. |
| u3 | Cover these verbs: search, status, doctor, add, scan, get, tree, remove, gc, conversation list, docs list, agents-start-here, and the failure surface for any `ok:false`. If a view type is missing a field you need, that is a CONTRACT gap: report it, render honestly without it. |
| u4 | THE FOUR-CASE MATRIX (ac-0001), per covered verb, through the REAL binary: piped with no flags → JSON; piped with --human → rendered; --json anywhere → JSON; FS3_OUTPUT=human → rendered. Model the tests on crates/cli/tests/envelope_goldens.rs, which already stands up a stub daemon serving frozen answers — reuse that shape (and its fixtures in crates/cli/tests/goldens/responses/) rather than inventing a second harness. Do NOT add a pty/expect dependency to test a real terminal without a PM ruling; FS3_OUTPUT is the deterministic stand-in for the tty leg and exists for exactly this reason. |
| u5 | ALLOWLIST GRANT, exact and exhaustive — for fs3-cli ONLY: comfy-table 8 (default-features=false, features=["custom_styling"]), owo-colors 4, anstream 1, textwrap 0.16 (default-features=false, features=["unicode-width","smawk","terminal_size"]). These are the rows LEARNINGS.md §1 justifies and nothing else is granted — indicatif, colored, tabled, ratatui and direct crossterm were all considered and DECLINED there, with reasons. Add the rows to the arch allowlist in the same commit as the dependency, and a fifth crate is a stop-and-ask. |
| u6 | ADD PROGRESS (Jordan's ruling, 2026-08-28, formally ruled at the freeze): `flowspace3 add` walks a whole repository before it answers, and in human mode it must show real progress — what is being scanned, with counts, not a frozen prompt and not a spinner that knows nothing. The honest source is u-w's stream: subscribe to GET /events and render scan_progress (root, root_path, files_seen, enqueued, current) while the POST is in flight. THE METER GOES TO STDERR, never stdout — stdout stays exactly the envelope it is today, which is what keeps the byte-goldens green by construction. u-w may not have landed when you build: develop against a recorded NDJSON fixture, and if /events is absent or errors, degrade SILENTLY to today's behaviour (no meter, no warning, no delay). In JSON mode there is no meter at all. |
| u7 | AGENT-PATH DOCS (ac-0005), same unit, same PR: AGENTS.md (CLAUDE.md is a symlink to it), /Users/jordanknight/substrate/flowspace/fs3-human-interface/.agents/skills/flowspace/SKILL.md, the agents-start-here page and the self-teaching CLI guidance under crates/cli/docs/. Each must state, explicitly: a TTY gets human output, a pipe/file/agent keeps getting JSON with no flag, `--json` forces JSON anywhere, and `FS3_OUTPUT=json` is how a harness whose terminal probe lies (an agent inside a tmux PTY looks exactly like a person) pins the machine shape once. An agent that reads only these docs must not be surprised by anything. |
